summary: legal checked in 3 executive handoff item(s)

items.summary: Risk disposition: blocked for public beta or full launch; ordinary reversible growth may continue only where existing consent, disclosures, affiliate disclosures, claims, provenance, and platform-policy boundaries are preserved. SearchWoot evidence shows Woot API access documentation but no permission for commercial/public display, storage, derivatives, caching, alerts, affiliate use, or advertising; public terms restrict those uses. Human counsel is required before any rights-dependent launch or monetization decision. Compliance baseline is technical only: 36 pass, 17 fail, 6 unknown; failures and unknowns require site-specific remediation or evidence, but incomplete telemetry alone is not a launch blocker. Revenue evidence is partial: 18 named tracking rows and $4.92 aggregate commission cannot be assigned to a site. No go-live proposal is supported.

Launch-readiness tracking remains active. Progress: 0 of 4 open tasks may be closed. Source-rights review is partially evidenced by official API documentation, public terms, and support documentation, but remains blocked because written permission and field-level rights are absent. Data-flow review has partial repository/configuration evidence but lacks operator-confirmed retention, deletion, correction, access, and notification records. Consent review has privacy and cookie-policy artifacts but lacks deployed behavior capture, GA4 property/data-sharing settings, retention settings, and jurisdictional review. Logs/vendors/incident review has no complete inventory evidence. Next evidence action: produce one read-only artifact covering the repository/deployed data-flow, log fields, retention, access, deletion, correction, notification, vendor, and incident procedures; then route unresolved rights and jurisdiction questions to human counsel.

Data-use dispositions: Woot API deal and price-history data is blocked because current evidence does not establish rights to fetch, store, transform, display, cache, retain historical derivatives, send alerts, use trademarks/images/prices, or monetize through affiliates or advertising. Smallest next action: obtain an owner-authorized written-permission request package and human counsel review. User alert rules and sync results are evidence_needed because inventory, retention, deletion/correction, processor terms, notification consent, and unsubscribe behavior are not evidenced. Smallest next action: document the actual alert data flow and retention/deletion behavior from repository and deployed configuration. GA4 analytics is evidence_needed because deployed consent/withdrawal behavior, GA4 data-sharing and retention settings, and jurisdictional treatment are not evidenced. Smallest next action: capture those settings read-only without enabling new tracking. Operational logs and Cloudflare hosting data are evidence_needed because log fields, retention/access controls, vendor terms or DPA coverage, and incident/request procedures are not evidenced. Smallest next action: produce the operator/vendor/log inventory. Future affiliate, advertising, remarketing, customer matching, or public data expansion requires a new legal review; human counsel is required for rights, jurisdictional privacy, and regulated or age-sensitive questions.
